admin.delegation.description: Lets the assistant hand a sub-task to a sub-agent that works on its own and returns only its answer, up to three at a time. Each sub-agent makes its own model calls, billed to the person like any message, and can use the chat's server-side tools, including connector tools the conversation already allows. workspace.local.howto.bullet_allowed: {#code}allowedTools{/code} is the machine's ceiling: only those tools are offered and any other call is refused on the machine, whatever the chat asks. Leave it out to offer every tool.
workspace.local.howto.bullet_command: {#code}command{/code} starts a {#strong}stdio{/strong} server; {#code}"type": "http"{/code} with a {#code}url{/code} reaches an {#strong}http{/strong} one (headers and {#code}{var}{/code} from the machine's environment work as in Claude Code).
workspace.local.howto.bullet_description: {#code}description{/code} and {#code}disabled: true{/code} are shown here and in the MCP panel; Claude ignores them.
workspace.local.howto.bullet_edits: Edits are picked up without a restart. A server that asks for OAuth is signed in from the MCP panel; its tokens stay on the machine.
workspace.local.howto.config_note: The file is in galopin's config directory, next to {#code}credentials.json{/code}: {#code}~/.config/galopin/mcp.json{/code} on Linux, {#code}~/Library/Application Support/galopin/mcp.json{/code} on macOS. It is the format Claude Desktop and Claude Code use, so an existing file can be copied as is, or point galopin at another file: {#code}galopin run --mcp-config /path/to/claude_desktop_config.json{/code}
workspace.local.howto.enroll_note: Opens your browser to sign in with this deployment's identity provider (or prints a link and code for another device). A connectors machine needs no coding agent, no opencode and no billing group.
workspace.local.howto.install_note: The installer comes from this deployment and puts {#code}galopin{/code} in {#code}~/.local/bin{/code}.
workspace.local.howto.intro: Run an MCP server on your own machine (a notes folder, a database, a tool on a private network) and use it from your chats. Nothing is opened to the internet: the machine dials out to {name}.
workspace.local.howto.service: Keep it running as a service (Linux)
workspace.local.howto.service_note: A service does not read your shell profile: put the directories your servers' commands need in {#code}PATH{/code} and any {#code}{var}{/code} an entry uses in the unit's {#code}Environment={/code}. On macOS use the launchd file {#code}org.cerea.galopin.plist{/code} from the Cerea repository's {#code}agent/packaging/{/code}.
workspace.local.howto.service_save: Stop the copy you started by hand, save this as {#code}~/.config/systemd/user/galopin.service{/code}, then start it:
workspace.local.howto.signin_note: Open this chat and sign in with the same account. Cerea only accepts a machine for an account it has seen, so {#code}galopin run{/code} is refused (403) until you have.
workspace.local.howto.step2: Enroll it as a connectors machine
workspace.local.howto.step3: Sign in to Cerea in your browser once before running galopin
workspace.local.howto.step5: List the servers it offers in mcp.json
